statement: Let W=sum_(i,j)d_ij[|ij>]-kappa[psi] with kappa>=0, all d_ij>=0, and psi=sum_i c_i|ii> in C4 tensor C4. If the Schmidt rank of psi is at most 3, every 2-block-positive W is decomposable for completely arbitrary d_ij. If all c_i are nonzero and d_ii=t*|c_i|^2 for a common real t, the same conclusion holds conditional on the unreviewed uniform-diagonal theorem frontier-20261028-uniform-diagonal-witness-nogo-v1.json SHA256 0cd207022ff7e81022def0a48c87766f4d4196d2cae6c5ae3cc6e6b23e731bf8. Offdiagonal d_ij remain arbitrary, and no product-metric assumption is made.
rank_at_most_three: Let I be the set of indices with c_i!=0, |I|<=3. W is the direct sum of its restriction to span{|ij>: i,j in I} and nonnegative diagonal terms on the orthogonal complement. The principal restriction remains 2-block positive. For |I|<=2 it is PSD, since every vector in its local support has Schmidt rank<=2. For |I|=3 it is the Choi operator of a 2-positive 3x3 map, and is decomposable by the known Yang-Leung-Tang theorem, https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.03534. Lifting its PSD and partial-transposed-PSD summands and adding the outside diagonal terms gives a decomposition of W on 4x4. This part does not depend on the new uniform-diagonal theorem.
full_schmidt_rank: For all c_i!=0 set F=diag(1/c_0,1/c_1,1/c_2,1/c_3). The invertible local congruence W'=(I tensor F)W(I tensor F)^* sends psi to omega=sum_i|ii>, sends d_ii to d_ii/|c_i|^2=t, and sends every offdiagonal coefficient to nonnegative d_ij/|c_j|^2. It preserves 2-block positivity. The cited uniform-diagonal theorem therefore gives W'=A+B^Gamma with A,B>=0. Inverting the local congruence, with the complex-conjugated inverse on B before applying Gamma, preserves decomposability. No characterization of unequal diagonal ratios d_ii/|c_i|^2 is claimed.
limits: Rank<=3 conclusion imports the established 3x3 theorem. The rank4 proportional-diagonal conclusion is conditional on the stated unreviewed all-parameter candidate. WRITTEN only, no novelty, general-witness classification, or 4x4 PPT/SN3 solution claim.
